subject: Post-call: spend constraints, batching levers, and next steps
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@clearline.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 09 Nov 2027 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap — spend constraints, batching levers, and next steps

Hi Samir — thanks again for the time today. Short recap from our side and proposed next steps so we stay aligned.

High-level summary
- Primary pain: production inference costs are outpacing projected budget as Clearline scales NLU for statement categorization and fraud signals.
- Key goals: fit inference into the mid-6-figure annual run-rate you mentioned without increasing model latency beyond 120ms p95, and preserve current quality (F1 drop <1.5%).
- Usage profile we heard: ~12M monthly inference tokens today (peaks to 20M) with heavy short-sequence traffic (median seq len ~40 tokens).

Cost levers we discussed (what we recommend testing first)
1) Batching + request coalescing: expect 20–35% per-token cost reduction on your traffic shape if we enable continuous batching with a 25ms window and adaptive batch size. Latency impact should be negligible for short sequences.
2) Prefix/KV caching for sessioned requests: should reduce repeated prefix compute for your 1:4 repeat-rate flows — estimate 10–18% savings for the policy-eval paths.
3) Quantization profile: a 4-bit dynamic quantized variant gives ~30% lower GPU cost but we’ll validate quality on the lending dataset.
4) Routing to a cost-tiered model for non-critical traffic: offload low-risk scoring to a smaller model variant during non-peak windows.

Immediate asks / next steps (owner / ETA)
- Clearline: share a 7-day token-level sample (anonymized) + two example conversation IDs for QA validation — Samir / procurement contact (by Fri 11/12).
- Redwood (Karthik): produce a short benchmark (batching + cache) against a 40-token median profile and share a simple cost sensitivity sheet (ETA: Wed 11/10 EOD). Attachment: preliminary estimate workbook.
- Redwood (Jonas): draft a pilot SOW with success metrics (cost reduction target, latency SLO, QA sample acceptance) and a two-week technical validation window (ETA: Tue 11/16).

Other notes
- Budget constraint: you cited a fixed budget envelope for Q1; we’ll structure the pilot to require minimal upfront spend and tie any committed capacity to measured savings.
- Procurement: if we get the sample dataset and your procurement contact in parallel, we can queue a redline review within 5 business days of pilot acceptance.

Attachments: clearline_inference_estimate_v1.xlsx (cost scenario rows + assumptions), call-recording-20271109.mp3

If this matches your read, I’ll kick off the benchmark and Jonas will start the SOW draft. Thanks — Hannah

--
Hannah Schmitt
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
hannah_schmitt@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0182

From: Samir Patel <samir@clearline.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@clearline.com, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Nov 2027 09:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — spend constraints, batching levers, and next steps

Thanks Hannah — concise and accurate. A couple quick clarifications from our side:

1) The 12M month token figure is current production; we expect 3x growth by June 2028 under the new feature rollout. The budget envelope I mentioned is $420k ARR for inference spend (hard cap unless we can show a 20–25% net saving through optimizations).
2) Latency: we can tolerate up to 150ms p95 for batch/async routes, but the interactive UI path must stay under 120ms p95.
3) About data: we'll anonymize the 7-day sample. I'll ask procurement to drop the sample in the shared Drive link and copy Karthik.

Two asks from us: can Redwood provide a simple ROI calc that models 3 growth scenarios (x1.5, x2, x3) vs batching + caching + 4-bit? Also, can you estimate expected SLA delta if we enable the smaller model routing (we need explicit fallback behaviour documented)?

I’ll push the sample this week and loop in our engineering manager to support the validation.

—Samir
Head of Product, Clearline Finance

On Wed, 10 Nov 2027 at 08:15, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com> wrote:
> Adding context on pilot structure and reporting metrics.
>
> From our experience, the fastest path to show budget impact is a 2-week technical validation where we:
> - Run continuous batching + KV cache on a mirrored traffic slice (no production rewrite),
> - Compare token throughput and per-token billed units against baseline,
> - Run a blind-quality check on a held-out sample (Clearline provides gold labels).
>
> Deliverables: cost sensitivity sheet (x1.5/x2/x3 scenarios), latency SLO table by route, and frank quality delta reporting. We can include an optional clause for an automatic downgrade to a higher-accuracy model if delta exceeds 1.5% F1.
>
> Jonas
> Senior Account Exec, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@clearline.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Nov 2027 15:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — spend constraints, batching levers, and next steps

Samir — quick technical note on the ROI calc and SLA delta you asked for.

ROI modeling approach (what I’ll run)
- Baseline: current per-token cost = estimate from your sample (we’ll normalize to per-1000 tokens).
- Levers modeled: batching (20–35% savings), KV cache (10–18% on targeted flows), 4-bit quant (25–33% depending on model family), routing to smaller model (15–25% for low-risk routes).
- Combined conservative case: assume only non-overlapping savings stack (expect ~40–45% realistic in short-term after pilot); aggressive stacking could show ~60% but we’ll present both.

SLA/quality delta notes
- Batching/windowing: p95 latent increase is typically <10–20ms for short sequences with our runtime.
- KV cache: negligible latency improvement for cached hits; miss penalty is small.
- 4-bit quant: quality risk depends on model and prompts — I’ll run a micro-eval against your two sample conversation IDs and surface any regression along with suggested prompt-engineering mitigations.
- Routing to smaller models: I’ll document fallback sequence (primary model -> fast small model -> full model fallback on quality warning) and expected cost profile; we’ll include an explicit rollback trigger in SOW.

I’ll attach the ROI slide and a short sensitivity worksheet to the HubSpot deal by Wed EOD. If we get the sample today, I can prioritize the micro-eval overnight.

Thanks — Karthik
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Great — thanks for the quick clarifications, Samir. Two logistical items:

1) When you drop the sample, please add a note of which endpoints are latency-sensitive vs batchable so we map routes correctly.
2) Procurement: if you can share any standard NDAs or procurement timelines upfront it speeds the pilot acceptance.

Jonas and Karthik will share the SOW and ROI sheet respectively by the dates above. I’ll set up a 30-minute follow-up next Tue (11/16) to review pilot metrics and sign-off criteria. Invite to follow.

Appreciate the clear constraints — we’ll make the pilot show measurable economics within the window.

Best,
Hannah
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
